full_judgment:
Bimalendu Bikash Roy Chowdhury,J: This is an application by the first defendant and the second defendant for release, of the Ship M.V. Golden Gate Ex Free Trader under arrest at the instance of the plaintiff. On or about August 10, 1992 the plaintiff brought the suit against the Ship, her owners and others claiming a sum of U.S.$ 398000 equivalent to Bangladesh Taka 1,55,22,000/, including interest thereon which he allegedly advanced to the fourth defendant; the original owner of the ship for payment of the outstanding claims of third parties who supplied necessaries to the ship. On August 13, 1992 he moved an application and obtained an ex-parte order from this court for arrest/attachment of the arrest contained a direction that "in the event the defendants can show that the principals are not liable for the amount claimed by the plaintiff in the suit or if the defendants furnish sufficient guarantees for the amount to the satisfaction of this Court, the order of arrest May be vacated." In Pursuance of this order the ship was arrested and attached the marshall of this court. The first defendant vessel and her owner, the second defendant have now entered appearance in the suit and filed a written objection against the plaintiffs application for arrest of the vessel. They also made an application for vacating the order of arrest on the ground that on his own pleading the plaintiff was not entitled to invoke the admiralty jurisdiction of this court in remand have the ship arrested under any of the provisions of the Admiralty Courts Act, 1861. It is submitted that the fourth defendant had, if at all, only borrowed the money to meet the demands of third parties and the plaintiff did not advance the money for procuring any necessaries supplied to the ship which is contemplated under Section 5 of the Act. 

 3. Admittedly, the nature  and scope of admiralty jurisdiction in Bangladesh is to be determined, with reference to the law in England as it stood in 1890 and for this purpose the statutory law is the Admiralty Courts Act, 186 Section 5 of the Act which is relevant for our purpose reads thus:- 

 In the instants case, the money claimed by the plaintiff from the defendants is by way of recovery of loan to the fourth defendant. The plaintiff does not claim that the payment was made for procuring any necessaries at or about the time when the necessaries were supplied to the ship. One might notice that the alleged necessaries were supplied several months before the loan was taken by the fourth defendant from the plaintiff and that the loan agreement does not also show that the loan was taken for payment to third parties supplying the necessaries. Thus, from the materials produced before me, it cannot be said that the plaintiffs claim has any nexus or proximity to the transaction of supply of necessaries, so as to bring the case within the ambit of Section 5 of the Admiralty Courts Act, 1861.
